sections.content: When most investors think about Midwest real estate, Chicago dominates the conversation. But savvy investors are quietly building serious wealth about 165 miles southwest in Peoria, Illinois. Real estate deals in Peoria IL offer something increasingly rare in today's market: affordability, cash flow, and a steady stream of motivated sellers. Whether you're a first-time wholesaler or a seasoned flipper expanding your portfolio, Peoria deserves a close look. If you're brand new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into this market breakdown.
Peoria IL Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Peoria is the largest city on the Illinois River and the county seat of Peoria County. With a population of around 113,000, it's a mid-sized city with a diverse economy anchored by healthcare, manufacturing, and education. Caterpillar Inc., one of the world's largest construction equipment manufacturers, has deep roots in the region, and OSF HealthCare and UnityPoint Health both operate major facilities here. These large employers create a stable base of working-class and middle-class renters — exactly the kind of tenant profile buy-and-hold investors love.

Peoria's real estate market is classified as a buyer's market, which is great news for investors. Days on market tend to run longer than national averages, giving you negotiating leverage. Foreclosure rates have historically been higher than the Illinois state average, which means distressed deal opportunities are plentiful if you know where to look. The [Peoria IL market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/peoria-il) at AIWholesail tracks current deal activity, median prices, and distressed property counts updated regularly.
Average Home Prices in Peoria IL

As of 2024, the median home price in Peoria sits around $105,000 to $125,000, depending on the neighborhood and property condition. This is dramatically lower than the national median of roughly $420,000, and it's what makes Peoria such an attractive market for investors with limited capital. Entry-level investment properties can often be acquired for $40,000 to $70,000, with after-repair values (ARVs) ranging from $90,000 to $150,000 in stabilized neighborhoods. Run your numbers using the free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate upside before you make an offer.

"The best real estate deals aren't always in the hottest markets. They're in the markets other investors overlook — places where the numbers work, the demand is real, and the competition hasn't driven prices into the stratosphere."
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Peoria
Not every zip code in Peoria makes sense for every strategy. Here's a quick breakdown of the key areas investors should know.
North Peoria and Peoria Heights

These areas sit on the north side of the city and into the suburbs and tend to attract more stable, owner-occupant buyers. Home values here range from $130,000 to $250,000+, making them ideal for fix-and-flip projects. Properties that need cosmetic updates — new kitchens, bathrooms, and flooring — can generate solid margins when purchased below market value.
South Side and Southtown

The south side offers the most affordable price points in the city, with many properties available in the $30,000 to $70,000 range. This is a prime zone for wholesale deals and value-add rentals. Gross rental yields in this area can exceed 15% to 20%, which is exceptional by any market's standards. Investors should be selective here — stick to streets with lower vacancy rates and properties close to schools or transit lines.
West Bluff and Richwoods

West Bluff is a historic neighborhood near Bradley University and offers strong rental demand driven by students and university employees. Richwoods is a more established residential area with solid resale values. Both neighborhoods offer a mix of flip and rental opportunities with relatively predictable exit strategies.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Peoria IL
Wholesaling

Peoria is a solid wholesale market. The volume of distressed, vacant, and inherited properties gives wholesalers consistent deal flow without competing against dozens of other buyers at every opportunity. Typical wholesale assignment fees in Peoria range from $5,000 to $15,000 per deal. Because cash buyer pools exist (local landlords are always looking for discounted rentals), moving contracts isn't difficult once you build your buyer's list. Read our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide to understand the full process before you start making offers.
Fix and Flip

Flipping works well in Peoria's north side and suburban neighborhoods where end buyers are active. A typical flip in Peoria might look like this: purchase price of $55,000, renovation budget of $35,000, ARV of $130,000. That leaves a gross profit of $40,000 before holding costs and closing fees — a respectable return for a mid-sized Midwest flip. The key is buying right. Use the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to model your maximum allowable offer before you commit to any property.
Buy and Hold Rentals

Rental demand in Peoria is strong. Roughly 47% of residents are renters, driven by a transient workforce, university population, and a significant portion of residents who can't qualify for mortgages. Average rents for a 3-bedroom single-family home range from $750 to $1,100 per month depending on condition and location. If you can acquire a property for $60,000 and rent it for $900 per month, your gross rent multiplier is under 6 — well inside the range of profitable long-term holds.

Pro Tip: In Peoria, target properties within 0.5 miles of major employers like OSF Saint Francis Medical Center or near Bradley University's campus. These micro-locations have lower vacancy rates and more stable tenant quality than properties in purely residential pockets of the south side.
Local Market Trends Investors Should Watch

items: Population shifts: Peoria has experienced gradual population decline over the past decade, which keeps prices low but also means you should be strategic about long-term hold positions in transitional neighborhoods.
Rising renovation costs: Like everywhere else, contractor labor and materials costs have increased since 2021. Budget at least 10% to 15% over your initial renovation estimate as a buffer.

Institutional interest growing: Small hedge funds and regional rental aggregators have started acquiring properties in secondary Midwest markets like Peoria, which could tighten deal flow and push prices up over the next 3 to 5 years — meaning now is still an early window.

Tax environment: Illinois property taxes are among the highest in the nation. Peoria County effective rates often run 2.5% to 3.5% of assessed value. Factor this into every rental cash flow analysis or you'll get burned.
Vacancy rates: City-wide vacancy hovers around 12% to 15%, higher than national averages. This reinforces the importance of neighborhood-level analysis rather than relying on city-wide statistics.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Peoria is attracting a growing number of out-of-state investors, particularly from California, Chicago, and the East Coast, who are priced out of their home markets. Here's how to approach this market remotely without getting burned.

items: Build a local team first: Before buying anything, identify a reliable property manager, a general contractor, and a real estate attorney licensed in Illinois. Your deal is only as good as the people executing it on the ground.
Drive the streets virtually: Use Google Street View to assess neighborhood conditions before flying out. Look for vacancy patterns, property upkeep, and proximity to commercial corridors.

Find off-market deals: The best Peoria deals rarely hit the MLS. Learn how to tap into distressed seller pipelines by reading our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).

Verify comps aggressively: Peoria's market has significant block-by-block variation. A comp two streets over can be wildly different in value. Always pull at least 5 to 7 recent sold comps within a quarter mile.
Understand Illinois landlord-tenant law: Illinois leans tenant-friendly. Eviction timelines can stretch 60 to 90 days in Peoria County. Price this risk into your cash flow projections.

Visit before your first deal: Even if you plan to invest remotely long-term, spend 2 to 3 days in Peoria for your first acquisition. Walking neighborhoods and meeting your contractor in person is worth more than any Zoom call.

Is Peoria IL the Right Market for You?

Peoria is not a glamorous market. It won't generate the social media buzz of Phoenix or Austin. But for investors focused on cash flow, affordable acquisitions, and building a rental portfolio without six-figure price tags, it checks a lot of boxes. The key is going in with realistic expectations, doing deep neighborhood-level research, and building a local team you trust. The investors quietly winning in Peoria right now started exactly the same way.
